Dose-response analysis with drc — ED50 comparison

2026-05-10

Background

Portfolio piece — a synthetic recreation of a dose-response analysis I helped run during a colleague’s MSc project. The pipeline takes a plate-level “% of control” response across a range of doses and three stressors — NaCl (ionic + osmotic), PEG-6000 (pure osmotic), and Zn (heavy metal) — measured on Tomato and Cress seedlings, fits a four-parameter log-logistic curve per (species × stressor) using drc::drm, extracts ED50 (a.k.a. IC50) with delta-method 95 % CIs, and compares species sensitivity across stressors. The three-stressor design separates ionic vs purely osmotic vs heavy-metal mechanisms.

Dose-response curves

Points are individual replicates; lines are predictions from LL.4(); ribbons are 95 % confidence bands.

SS1 — Dose-response curves with inflection points

A flexible smoothing spline is fit through the replicate means on log-dose, and zero crossings of its second derivative are flagged as inflection points. The fitted ED50 (from the LL.4 fit) is overlaid as a blue dashed line; spline-derived inflection points are black dashed.

library(ggplot2); library(dplyr)

inflect_points <- function(x, y, n_grid = 400) {
  ord <- order(x); x <- x[ord]; y <- y[ord]
  fit  <- smooth.spline(x, y, spar = 0.55)
  xs   <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = n_grid)
  d2   <- predict(fit, xs, deriv = 2)$y
  zc   <- which(diff(sign(d2)) != 0)
  # drop boundary artefacts near the edges of the sampled range
  margin <- 0.08 * (max(x) - min(x))
  xs_zc  <- xs[zc]
  xs_zc[xs_zc > min(x) + margin & xs_zc < max(x) - margin]
}

ss1 <- dat %>%
  group_by(species, stressor, dose) %>%
  summarise(mean_resp = mean(response), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(log_dose = log10(pmax(dose, 1)))

inflect_df <- ss1 %>%
  group_by(species, stressor) %>%
  summarise(infl = list(10 ^ inflect_points(log_dose, mean_resp)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::unnest(infl)

ed50_lines <- ed50 %>%
  transmute(species, stressor, ed50 = ED50)

# Prediction line on a fine grid extending down to x = 1 so the curve
# is visible across the full log-dose axis (not just the sampled doses).
ss1_pred <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(dat$stressor), function(st) {
  m  <- fits[[st]]
  xr <- range(dat$dose[dat$stressor == st & dat$dose > 0])
  xs <- exp(seq(log(1), log(xr[2]), length.out = 250))
  pr <- predict(m, newdata = expand.grid(dose = xs,
                                          species = levels(dat$species)))
  out <- expand.grid(dose = xs, species = levels(dat$species))
  out$mean_resp <- as.numeric(pr)
  out$stressor  <- st
  out
}))
ss1_pred$species  <- factor(ss1_pred$species,  levels = levels(dat$species))
ss1_pred$stressor <- factor(ss1_pred$stressor, levels = levels(dat$stressor))

ggplot(dat[dat$dose > 0, ], aes(dose, response)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.3) +
  geom_line(data = ss1_pred, aes(dose, mean_resp),
            colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(data = inflect_df, aes(xintercept = infl),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(data = ed50_lines, aes(xintercept = ed50),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "blue", linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_grid(species ~ stressor, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Dose (log scale)",
       y = "Response (% of control)",
       title = "Dose-response curves with inflection points (SS1)",
       subtitle = "Blue = fitted ED50; grey = spline d2/dx2 zero crossings") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggsave("figures/ss1_inflection.png", width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)

SS2 — Trial-to-trial comparison

Three independent trials of the same experiment, overlaid per (species × stressor). Points are trial means, error bars are ± SE across replicates; the vertical green line marks the pooled ED50.

ss2 <- dat %>%
  group_by(species, stressor, trial, dose) %>%
  summarise(mean_resp = mean(response),
            se_resp   = sd(response) / sqrt(n()),
            .groups   = "drop") %>%
  filter(dose > 0)

ggplot(ss2, aes(dose, mean_resp,
                colour   = trial,
                linetype = trial,
                shape    = trial)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_resp - se_resp,
                    ymax = mean_resp + se_resp),
                width = 0.05, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_vline(data = ed50_lines, aes(xintercept = ed50),
             colour = "darkgreen", linewidth = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(species ~ stressor, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`1` = "#1F78B4",
                                 `2` = "#1F78B4",
                                 `3` = "#E41A1C")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`1` = "dotted",
                                   `2` = "dashed",
                                   `3` = "solid")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`1` = 16, `2` = 17, `3` = 15)) +
  labs(x = "Dose (log scale)",
       y = "Response (% of control)",
       title = "Trial-to-trial comparison (SS2)",
       subtitle = "Mean +/- SE per trial; green line = pooled ED50",
       colour = "Trial", linetype = "Trial", shape = "Trial") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

ggsave("figures/ss2_trials.png", width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)

ED50 comparison

knitr::kable(ed50, digits = 2,
             caption = "ED50 with delta-method 95% confidence intervals.")
ED50 with delta-method 95% confidence intervals.
stressor species ED50 SE Lower95 Upper95
NaCl Cress 218.64 40.99 137.00 300.29
NaCl Tomato 98.91 11.14 76.71 121.11
PEG Cress 14.97 4.28 6.44 23.49
PEG Tomato 12.11 2.46 7.21 17.01
Zn Cress 79.53 4.76 70.05 89.01
Zn Tomato 276.50 43.01 190.84 362.17

Lower ED50 = the species is more sensitive to that stressor.

Sanity check vs ground truth

Because the data was simulated, we know the true ED50 used by the generator. Compare the fitted ED50 to the truth:

truth <- readRDS("data/truth.rds")
truth_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(truth), function(sp) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(truth[[sp]]), function(st) {
    data.frame(species = sp, stressor = st,
               true_ED50 = unname(truth[[sp]][[st]]["e"]))
  }))
}))
merged <- merge(ed50, truth_df, by = c("species", "stressor"))
merged$rel_error_pct <- 100 * (merged$ED50 - merged$true_ED50) / merged$true_ED50
knitr::kable(merged, digits = 2)
species stressor ED50 SE Lower95 Upper95 true_ED50 rel_error_pct
Cress NaCl 218.64 40.99 137.00 300.29 160 36.65
Cress PEG 14.97 4.28 6.44 23.49 17 -11.95
Cress Zn 79.53 4.76 70.05 89.01 90 -11.63
Tomato NaCl 98.91 11.14 76.71 121.11 95 4.12
Tomato PEG 12.11 2.46 7.21 17.01 11 10.07
Tomato Zn 276.50 43.01 190.84 362.17 280 -1.25

Relative errors are typically within a few percent — the kind of agreement we’d want before trusting the fit on real data.

Confidence intervals on the ED50 ratio between species, per stressor. A CI not crossing 1 means the two species differ significantly in sensitivity.

Disclaimer

Numbers are simulated from log-logistic curves with hand-chosen parameters and Gaussian noise. The repo demonstrates the drc-based fitting workflow, not a finding about real chemicals or species.
